Find the inverse of $f(x) = 3x-5$, and verify by computing $f(f^{-1}(x))$.
questions.answer: Swap and solve: $x=3y-5 \Rightarrow y=\frac{x+5}{3}$, so $f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x+5}{3}$. Check: $f(f^{-1}(x)) = 3\cdot\frac{x+5}{3}-5 = x+5-5=x$. ✓

sections.heading: Average rate of change (a preview of the derivative)

questions.q: Find the average rate of change of $f(x)=x^2$ over $[1,4]$, and interpret this as the slope of a secant line.
questions.answer: $\frac{f(4)-f(1)}{4-1}=\frac{16-1}{3}=5$ — this is the slope of the secant line connecting $(1,1)$ and $(4,16)$.

questions.q: For $f(x)=x^2$, find the average rate of change over $[1,1+h]$ in terms of $h$, and describe what happens as $h\to0$ (a preview of the derivative).
questions.answer: $\frac{f(1+h)-f(1)}{h}=\frac{(1+h)^2-1}{h}=\frac{2h+h^2}{h}=2+h$. As $h\to0$, this approaches $2$ — the instantaneous rate of change (derivative) of $f$ at $x=1$.
